rows.note: This is the all-purpose verb for projecting liquid or another substance outward in fine drops, including spraying something onto a target.

example.english: I spray the flowers in the garden with a hose.
example.jyutping: ngo5 jung6 seoi2 hau4 pan3 faa1 jyun2 di1 faa1

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for a fine, dispersed liquid mist.

example.english: I spray a little mist on my face in the morning, so my skin is less dry.
example.traditional: 朝早噴少少噴霧喺面上，皮膚冇咁乾。
example.jyutping: ziu1 zou2 pan3 siu2 siu2 pan3 mou6 hai2 min6 soeng5 pei4 fu1 mou5 gam3 gon1

rows.note: Use this specifically for the pressurized can or container that releases a spray.

example.english: This spray can has run out of pressure, so nothing comes out when I press it.
example.traditional: 呢枝噴霧罐冇晒氣，撳極都噴唔出。
example.jyutping: ni1 zi1 pan3 mou6 gun3 mou5 saai3 hei3 gam6 gik6 dou1 pan3 m4 ceot1

rows.note: Use this for a small flowering or berry-bearing branch, rather than a whole bouquet.

example.english: That flower stall has some lovely spray of flowers, so I bought one to put in a small vase.
example.traditional: 花墟嗰檔有啲靚花枝，我買返去插喺細樽度。
example.jyutping: faa1 heoi1 go2 dong3 jau5 di1 leng3 faa1 zi1 ngo5 maai5 faan1 heoi3 caap3 hai2 sai3 zeon1 dou6
